name: MACBA (Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona)
funding: €13.2M budget. Consortium comprising the Generalitat de Catalunya, Ajuntament de Barcelona, Spanish Ministry of Culture, and Fundació MACBA.
watch: Repsol is a fossil-fuel funder; Naturgy executives on the board.
why_flagged: Repsol is a fossil-fuel funder; Naturgy executives on the board.
records_note: MACBA posts its 2025 general accounts and audit reports for 2011 to 2018 and names its trustees, but no annual report or donor list.

name: MacKenzie Art Gallery
funding: Canada Council, Saskatchewan Arts Board, City of Regina, Sask Lotteries. 2024-25 corporate sponsors: TD Ready Commitment ($200k+), Rawlco Radio, RBC Foundation, Canada Life, SaskTel.
watch: TD Bank, the largest corporate sponsor, pleaded guilty on 10 October 2024 to money-laundering conspiracy and Bank Secrecy Act failures, with about $3B in penalties.
records_note: Posts annual reports and signed financial statements for each year from 2014-15 to 2025-26, names sponsors and donors in the 2024-25 report, lists trustees.

name: MACRO (Museo d'Arte Contemporanea di Roma)
funding: €3.5M budget. Roma Capitale municipal cultural council and Azienda Speciale Palaexpo public agency.

name: Madre · museo d'arte contemporanea Donnaregina
funding: Fondazione Donnaregina, funded by the Campania region.
records_note: No annual report; the foundation's transparency portal posts accounts 2019 to 2026 and names its board, while the site lists no sponsors or donors.

name: MAIIAM
funding: Privately held by the Beurdeley-Bunnag family: Jean Michel Beurdeley, the late Patsri Bunnag and son Eric Bunnag Booth.
watch: First private contemporary art museum in Chiang Mai, Thailand. Founded by Jean Michel Beurdeley and Eric Bunnag Booth in memory of Chao Chom Iam.
records_note: The site publishes no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; it names only the Beurdeley-Bunnag family as founders.

name: MAK - Museum of Applied Arts
funding: 2024: EUR 16.1M income, EUR 11.7M of it federal base funding; sponsors Porsche Holding Salzburg, Wienerberger, Wiener Städtische, Swarovski and others.
watch: Porsche Holding Salzburg, a VW Group firm, began a multi-year partnership in 2024; 174,476 visitors in 2024.
records_note: The MAK posts annual reports for 2017 to 2025, audited accounts, a named 2024 sponsor thank-you list and its Kuratorium members.

name: Makan Art Space
funding: Founded 2003; rentals and screenings, then grants from AFAC and SIDA.
watch: Artist-run; unclear whether it still operates.
records_note: Makan's old website is gone and no reports, accounts, funders or board are posted anywhere found.

name: Malmö Konsthall
funding: Municipal kunsthalle run by the City of Malmö.
records_note: No records of its own; parent Malmö stad posts its 2025 annual report with accounts; no funder list, no board found.

name: MAMbo
funding: Municipal museum of the City of Bologna.
records_note: The museum's own sites could not be read, so its reports, accounts, funders and board stay unchecked.

name: Manege Central Exhibition Hall
funding: City: St Petersburg state budgetary institution under the Committee for Culture; director Anna Yalova (acting from Sep 2022, confirmed Feb 2023).
watch: Site has no partners page; 2024 shows (Pushkinskaya-10 retrospective, Polytechnic Museum) credited to the Committee for Culture.
records_note: Names partners and sponsors in text with no date and lists a four-member supervisory board; posts only a 2025 task report and a financial plan.

name: Marres, House for Contemporary Culture
funding: Mondriaan Fund, Province of Limburg, Municipality of Maastricht; non-profit foundation.

name: Matadero Madrid
watch: Former municipal slaughterhouse, now a large public creation center for collaborative arts and ecological thought.
